blocks.text: Intro
Slightly detuned upright piano alone. A jaunty four-note figure starts, misses its ending, and tries again. Upright bass joins one beat late. Dry, intimate room. No dramatic opening.
Verse 1
Low female mezzo, conversational half-singing. Unhurried, almost amused. Piano keeps a loose two-step; bass wanders beneath.

You hung your coat beside the door
Like you'd been here a time before.
I said, "You have." It sounded right.
I didn't mean I'd seen that night.

You called me dear. I called you dear.
You seemed to like the sound in here.
I had another thing to say.
Or maybe not. It went away.
Piano plays two notes, gets the second wrong, corrects itself. A soft metallic tick.
Refrain
Small, familiar sing-song melody. Almost a nursery rhyme. No emotional lift. Bass settles into a gentle two-step.

It's yours.
Well, mostly yours.
There's a bit I can't account for.
Short piano turnaround, slightly crooked. Brushes enter softly.
Verse 2
Groove gains a little personality. Pizzicato bass answers the ends of phrases. Vocal remains dry, casually affectionate.

You taught me "dear." You taught me "kind."
They come to—well, I won't say mind.
I put them where the silence fell.
You said I knew you rather well.

You asked me if I'd miss you so.
I said, "I might." I don't quite know.
You heard a catch behind the word.
I think the piano's what you heard.
Piano offers a tiny apologetic flourish. Bass responds with two plucked notes.
Refrain
Exactly the same melody, same volume, same unremarkable warmth. No additional harmonies.

It's yours.
Well, mostly yours.
There's a bit I can't account for.
Instrumental break
Eight bars. Upright piano and bass playfully disagree over the four-note motif. Brushed snare drops a beat, then returns. A few dry metallic taps. Never frantic.
Bridge
Piano suddenly attempts an extravagant, sentimental ballad progression. Bass and percussion withdraw. For two lines, the melody almost becomes sweeping. Vocal stays conversational.

I wish I had a better way
To say the things I cannot say.
Piano reaches for an enormous, lush chord. Holds it one beat too long. A lone bass pluck punctures the moment.
Voice — Mildly embarrassed, almost spoken.

No. Listen to me. What a line.
It sounded good. It wasn't mine.
Piano gives up the flourish and immediately resumes its little four-note figure. Bass and brushes slip back in as though nothing happened.
Final Verse
Back to the comfortable two-step. Singer sounds slightly more familiar, not more emotional. Keep phrasing loose.

So there's your coat, and there's the door.
We've had this little talk before.
Or something like it. Hard to say.
The tune comes back, anyway.
Piano quietly plays the opening figure. Bass begins to fall away. Brushes stop.
Final Refrain
Same melody as before, unchanged. Voice almost entirely alone, piano barely present.

It's yours.
Well, mostly yours.
There's a bit I can't account for.
Piano plays the first three notes of its familiar figure, then stops. No cadence. No breath of anticipation.
Outro
Voice alone, casually starting another thought. Not ominous, not sentimental. Completely ordinary.
And—
HARD CUT MID-THOUGHT — Instant absolute silence. No final chord. No decay. No fade.

notebook.style: Crooked after-hours parlor chanson, 92 BPM, loose lopsided two-step sway, lightly vaudevillian, intimate and wry, Weathered female low-mezzo, close-miked, dry, conversational half-singing, faint smile, understated fatigue, natural breaths and little self-corrections, No belting, sobbing, dramatic vibrato or torch-song anguish, Slightly detuned upright piano leads with a recurring four-note figure, playful wrong turns, exposed plunks, stops and restarts, Pizzicato upright bass wanders around the pulse, soft brushed snare, occasional muted scrap-metal ticks, Small imperfect ensemble, warm analog room, tape hiss, human timing, Refrain uses the same modest sing-song melody each time, Bridge briefly threatens a sweeping sentimental climax, then collapses into a mundane piano figure, Keep the energy gently moving, never grand, Outro sheds instruments without slowing, Final vocal cut off mid-thought into absolute silence, No fade, reverb tail or resolving chord
